messages:
Maya (Sales): Hi team — onboarding note for Nimbus Inc POC. They want a 99th <= 300ms SLA for chat during 9-5, ability to burst to ~1k qps for marketing events, and nightly embedding batches (80k items over 6h). Also sent security questionnaire (SAML + KMS + SIEM export). Thoughts on reserved vs pooled burst strategy?

Omar (Solutions): Main tradeoff: full reservation gives predictable latency (easy to hit 99th) but higher committed cost. Hybrid: reserve baseline to cover 60-70% of expected steady qps, plus a burst pool with pre-purchased burst credits for spikes. They also want prewarming before product demos.

Priya (Runtime): Quick capacity calc from their traffic CSV: median 320 qps, 95th 640, peaks 1k for 15-30m. My proposal:
- Model: rwd-3b-int8 for chat (optimized kernels)
- Baseline reserve: 4 x A40 equiv (gives headroom to hit 95/99 for steady 640-ish)
- Burst: 3 x prewarmed GPUs in a burst pool to cover the 1k spikes (fast-add)
- Embeddings: split nightly into 3 parallel workers on spot instances, concurrency-limited to avoid impacting daytime pools

Priya (Runtime): Autoscale policy suggestion:
- Metric: tail latency (p99) + queue depth + GPU util
- Scale-up trigger: p99 > 250ms for 30s OR queue depth > 100
- Scale-down: cooldown 10m after p99 < 200ms and util < 40%
- Max multiplier: 6x baseline; fallback policy: route to quantized fallback model (rwd-1.3b-q4) when burst exhausted

Diego (Ops): Contracting/billing notes: preheat runs that occur while reserved capacity exists are not billed extra. Burst GPU use billed against burst credits or metered at on-demand rate if credits exhausted. We can offer a monthly burst credits bucket that resets. Need legal to sign off on metric definitions for SLA.

Maya (Sales): @Diego can you confirm how preheat will be scheduled (who triggers) and whether demos count as preheat? Need client clarity.

Diego (Ops): Preheat should be scheduled through console API or via our SRE-runbook; demos we can include as part of preheat allowance if arranged 48h in advance. I'll add a clause for a limited number of ad-hoc preheats per month.

AuditBot: security-audit: Received questionnaire Nimbus_Sec_Q_2026.pdf. Required items flagged: SAML integration, KMS CMKs, SIEM log sink, key rotation evidence.

Omar (Solutions): For SAML we can do IdP federation for console access. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated & Private; logs can be exported to their SIEM via our log-forwarder. Need to prepare a short appendix showing evidence and how to configure.

Claire (Legal): SLA language reminder: be precise about how p99 is computed (per-route vs overall), windowing, and exclusion clauses for force majeure, preheat, and chaos-testing. I'll draft SLA addendum after we lock numbers.

Priya (Runtime): Preheat script snippet (for KV / prefix warm):
```bash
# preheat KVCACHE using representative prompts
while read PROMPT; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-int8","input":"'$PROMPT'","max_tokens":24}' &
done < preheat_prompts.txt
wait
```

Priya (Runtime): Also recommending a rehearsal: run preheat 48h before demo, then 30m before demo as a short burst. Monitor p99, KV hit rate, and cold-start counts.

Maya (Sales): Client also asked about quality delta when falling back to rwd-1.3b-q4. Omar/Priya can we produce a 1-page eval: latency vs coherence tradeoff on their sample prompts? They sent 300 seed prompts attached.

Omar (Solutions): I can run an eval against 200 sample prompts overnight and produce a short CSV with per-prompt scores (BLEU-ish + human flagged failure cases). We'll add recommended thresholds for when fallback is acceptable.

Diego (Ops): Infra note: we'll provision reservation res-4309 and tag it Nimbus-prod. Need network checklist: NAT egress, allowed IP ranges, and peering setup window. I'll post checklist in shared drive.

Priya (Runtime): Also add an automated fallback route in the router policies: if latency SLO breaches AND burst pool unavailable, switch to fallback model with forced temperature 0.2 and reduced max_tokens to control cost. Include a header in responses to indicate model variant for downstream auditing.

Maya (Sales): Next steps: (1) Diego creates reservation + contract language for burst credits, (2) Priya runs KV warm script & contributes preheat rehearse plan, (3) Omar runs eval on 200 prompts, (4) Claire to draft SLA appendix. I'll send Nimbus the draft plan and scheduling options.

Maya (Sales): resolving for now, will reopen when Nimbus replies or when legal has the SLA draft. :white_check_mark:
